summary: Switching an item from the keyboard in Source-linked flow loses focus during the loading transition and never restores it to the originating flow control.
fix: Capture the focused control/region before hiding selected content and retain that focus token across loading messages. Restore it only when the matching completed selection is visible, unless the user deliberately moved focus; alternatively keep navigation controls outside the hidden data region. Add a flow-button -> loading -> loaded focus regression alongside the existing moment-focus test.
evidence: D6.2 says a new pause preserves keyboard focus and D6.5 says updates preserve focus. studyClient executes "element('selected').hidden = message.loading" at 72, but reads document.activeElement only later at 90-91 and then tries to focus a rebuilt flow button inside the hidden region at 96. The actual generated context HTML was exercised with Playwright CLI against the existing deterministic QA host: focus #flow button[data-item=browser], Enter, qaPublish(loading), qaPublish(history). Result: before BUTTON/browser/flow; during BODY; after BODY; focusPreserved:false. Evidence: artifacts/cycle-0006/review/pass1-design-focus.txt. This reproduces the webview loading/focus defect; it does not assert native editor visual acceptance. Existing 22-check QA only verifies moment focus on a non-loading update.
